cosmos_B3:
Edit the supplied B2 image as a tightly scoped star-organization study. Preserve its exact camera, composition, central axis, gigantic inverted mountain silhouette, narrow vertical fissure, thick square terraces and their corners, monumental outer-circle trajectories, floating rock silhouettes, foreground walkway, broken railings, wet reflections, and both people, especially their connected hands, braced legs and body weight. Preserve the existing crimson patch and rock treatment. Do not solve the image by weakening the cosmic spectacle or changing the geometry.
Change only the distribution and internal organization of stars and galaxies within the existing sky and ring bands. Keep the universe vast, brilliant, solemn and overwhelming. Retain the three dominant existing depth bands and their present routes around the mass. Give each band a distinct grouping grammar. The lowest visible outer sweep is nearest: concentrate its light into a few large, sharp, wedge-shaped star clusters, with clear leading nodes and subordinate smaller lights. The middle belt has separated constellational groups of paired or tripled bright nodes and compact satellite clouds. The distant upper sweep uses finer, smaller, softer chains of stars, partially disappearing behind the existing mountain and terrace silhouettes. The bands must remain spatially separated, not merge into one luminous flat disk.
Redistribute much of the currently uniform off-band star confetti INTO the bright groups instead of simply deleting their energy. Between the belts and between major groups, create distinct cold-black corridors with only rare isolated points; keep brilliant dense clusters and the huge outer sweep. Make the unequal spacing look ordered by membership and depth, not random scattering. Preserve the centered cosmogram and its solemn axial order while varying the internal rhythm of its sectors. Replace the repeated similarly prominent spiral galaxies with a clear hierarchy: one dominant oblique spiral nested within a middle-belt group on the right, a smaller subordinate elliptical cluster on the left, and remaining spirals absorbed into much smaller satellite knots. Do not place a similar hero galaxy in every corner.
Convey depth through different star scales, sharpness, density, and clean existing occlusion boundaries. No stars should paint over solid dark terrace faces, the figures, or their hands. Keep the hand contact and supported stance readable. Maintain the current high-contrast cold-black and luminous-white intensity. Do not introduce text, labels or additional objects. This is a focused reorganization of the same grand cosmic image, not a new scene.
pattern_A_liquid:
Edit the three-cell motif in the central “2 SPINE-END UNION” panel of the reference. Produce one isolated revised motif, solid black on a clean white background. Do not reproduce the page, labels, construction diagrams, or size examples.
This is a tightly bounded silhouette revision, not a new emblem. Preserve the exact structural idea: one connected backbone, three unequal-sized cells in the same order, approximately 1 : 0.8 : 0.65 from top to bottom. All three cavities open to the right. Each cell has two unequal arms on the same side of its backbone. Only the longer upper arm turns inward once to form a single hook. The shorter lower arm ends in a simple tapered point without curling. The staggered tips leave an oblique open mouth. Every white cavity must remain visibly connected to the outside background.
Make one dominant change: replace the rectilinear construction contour with a controlled, directional liquid silhouette. Let the backbone follow one shallow sweep rising toward the upper right, with the largest upper cell leading and the smallest lower cell trailing. Give each outer shoulder a rounded, weighted bulge near its root, then smoothly narrow the long arm toward its one inward hook. Curve the inner shoulder transitions without making the cavity circular or closing its mouth. Taper the short arm cleanly. Use broad convex masses and restrained concave transitions, not decorative ripples.
Keep the two short spine-end connections, but blend their contours smoothly into the same backbone so that the result reads as one flowing body rather than three letters attached by exposed little posts. Never connect an arm tip to the next cell. Keep the backbone and connections robust enough to remain continuous when reduced.
The liquid impression must come entirely from contour, directional weight, and taper. Use flat, fully opaque black only. No highlights, gradients, glow, transparency, extra outlines, texture, droplets, splashes, floating fragments, additional branches, new cavities, or more cells. Avoid an evenly toothed comb, stacked block letters, a feather, fish skeleton, flame ornament, or circular crest. Preserve the compactness and open negative spaces of the original. Do not add a character, garment, weapon, scenery, or any implied magical function.
